neighbours.label: main verb directly following a first-person subject ('I'/'we', incl. 'I have read', 'I just finished', 'we may worthily enter'), often formal/religious or letter-style first-person statements
fire: Dear editor, I have read your article on river pollution twice and I must respond to it.
Hi! I found your lovely blog while searching for old family recipes last night.
We implore Thee, Lord, that with humble hearts we may worthily enter into Thy presence.
Dear Mr. Smith, I just finished reading your book on grammar and wanted to thank you.
Sit at my right hand until I make thine enemies a footstool for thy feet.
Last summer I visited my grandmother in Lisbon and learned to bake bread with her.
Thank you for the kind note; I received your parcel this morning in perfect condition.
Before the meeting began, I asked the chairman whether the minutes had been approved.
quiet: Dear editor, your article on river pollution has been read by many people in our town.
The lovely blog about old family recipes was shared widely among the members last night.
Lord, grant that pure hearts be given to all who come into Thy presence.
Your book on grammar arrived yesterday and the students seem to like it a great deal.
The grandmother in Lisbon taught her neighbours to bake bread every summer.
The parcel arrived this morning in perfect condition, according to the porter.
Before the meeting began, the chairman checked whether the minutes had been approved.
Many readers found the new edition of the novel more satisfying than the first.

notes: Label and sentences written blind by a Claude subagent from the card text alone (prompt: haiku_labeler/prompt.md, identical for Haiku, Sonnet and Opus); one retry on mechanical checks. Part of a Haiku/Sonnet/Opus comparison on the same 48 poles.
